newsitem.title: USA: COM/Electric details power auction proposal.
newsitem.headline: COM/Electric details power auction proposal.

text.p: Commonwealth Energy System said Friday details of its plan calling for the auction of the company's power supply were presented to Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities on March 31.

The plan was submitted jointly by the system's three electric utility subsidiaries -- Commonwealth Electric Co, Cambridge Electric Light Co and Canal Electric Co -- collectively referred to as COM/Electric.
In leaving the power supply business, COM/Electric will continue to provide local electric distribution services, The company said.
The presentation continues COM/Electric's continued efforts to respond to the state's call for the creation of a competitive market for electricity, the company said.

"Over the next several months we will be submitting a formal filing to the state DPU for permission to carry out our auction which, we believe, offers customers the greatest mitigation of stranded costs and best opportunity to benefit from a competitiae power market," the company said.
In February 1996, it noted, COM/Electric became the first electric utility in Massachusetts to propose to voluntarily leave the power supply business.

Since then, most of the state's other utilities and regulatory bodies have adopted COM/Electric's approach to creating a system of electricity production companies and separate distribution companies with the aim of providing customers with the opportunity to receive lower electric bills.

COM/Electric's plan calls for the use of two different types of auctions, Commonwealth Energy said, explaining this will allow the highest and most accurate market value to be established for its 18 power supply contracts and six generating plants.

For the sale of all 18 of its power contracts, COM/Electric has developed an ascending-bid auction, patterned after the recent auctioning of radio spectrum licenses by the Federal Communications Commission.

The auction will use internet based auction software for a bid process that is expected to be staged over a multi-week period. The auction, which will look for the highest total price, will sell individual contracts, groups of contracts, or custom-tailored, bidder-selected groups of contracts.
A full description of the contracts, a pre-bid meeting, and instruction on the software will be offered prior to the auction, Commonwealth Energy said.

A second auction, using sealed bids, will be held for the sale of COM/Electric's generating assets. These include Canal Station Unit One and one-half of Unit Two in Sandwich, diesel generators on Martha's Vineyard, and the Kendall and Blackstone generating plants in Cambridge.
